# exa-search-cli

> CLI for Exa neural search, URL crawling, and deep research from terminal. Built for developers, scripts, and AI agents that need clean JSON output.

## Install

```bash
uv tool install exa-search-cli
```

or:

```bash
pip install exa-search-cli
```

Get API key at: https://exa.ai (free tier available)

## Commands

- `exa-search <query>` — neural web search. Flags: --json, --compact, --num-results, --type, --category, --start-date, --end-date, --include-domain, --exclude-domain, --similar <url>, --text, --max-chars, --objective, --max-age-hours
- `exa-crawl <url>` — fetch readable text or focused excerpts. Flags: --json, --compact, --max-chars, --query, --max-age-hours
- `exa-research <topic>` — AI deep research task. Flags: --json, --model
- `exa-research-status <research-id>` — check status / fetch result of a research task. Flags: --json

## Categories for exa-search --category

publication, people, company, news, personal site, financial report; legacy flags: tweet, github, paper, research paper, pdf, linkedin profile

## Best for

- AI agents
- search automation
- terminal workflows
- JSON output
- developer productivity

## Quick examples

```bash
exa-search "transformer architecture" --category publication --json
exa-search --similar https://github.com/astral-sh/uv --json
exa-crawl https://example.com -c 8000
exa-research "current state of quantum error correction" --json
exa-research-status r_01k... --json
```

## JSON output

exa-search returns: results[]{title, url, published_date, author, highlights[], text}
exa-crawl returns: results[]{url, title, text}
exa-research / exa-research-status return: {research_id, model, instructions, status, output.content, error}
Agent-safe jq result iterator: (if type=="array" then . else (.results // []) end)[]

## Research workflow (0.1.6)

- `--category publication`: scholarly sources; paper/research paper map to publication.
- Current types include auto, lite, fast, instant, deep-lite, deep, deep-reasoning; legacy keyword/neural remain accepted.
- `exa-search QUERY --text --max-chars 8000 --json`: bounded text per result; text and highlights are not requested together.
- `exa-crawl URL1 URL2 -c 12000 --json`: batch up to 100 URLs in one request; terminal output honors -c.
- All commands: --timeout SECONDS (default 60), --version. No automatic retries.
- Invalid arguments exit 2 before network calls; API failures exit nonzero with stderr diagnostics and redacted keys.
- Crawl JSON preserves per-URL statuses; partial failures warn on stderr, all failures exit 1.
- Search is discovery, not bibliographic verification; confirm metadata at the primary source. Crawl extracts text, not original PDF files.

## Focused retrieval

- `exa-search QUERY --objective "Prefer original pricing pages, not directories" --compact`: supplies the broader research goal. Objective is 1–4096 characters, not blank, and incompatible with --similar. Preferences do not replace hard filters or source validation.
- `exa-crawl URL --query "specific question" -c 2500 --compact`: extracts relevant passages from across a long page, with full text explicitly disabled. Do not assume excerpts contain all qualifications.
- Search and crawl support `--max-age-hours`: omitted = API defaults; -1 = cache only; 0 = fresh fetch; 1–720 = maximum cache age. This controls content age, not publication date. Search type lite does not support the flag.
- Search and crawl support `--compact`: implies JSON; one line; removes empty/decorative fields and duplicate URL IDs, while retaining evidence, substantive extended fields, costs, warnings and statuses. Ordinary --json remains unchanged.
- Bounded full text reaching its cap warns on stderr that content may be incomplete. No automatic paid refetch or implicit state is added.
